stem: After a wrong-site surgery, a hospital performs a root cause analysis. What is the primary purpose of this process?

options.A: Identify the individual closest to the event and assign direct blame because personal fault is the main target of root cause analysis after a sentinel event.
options.B: Document the event for legal purposes without changing care processes because root cause analysis is separate from efforts to prevent recurrence.
options.C: Determine whether the event can be removed from internal reports because the main goal is to reduce the number of documented sentinel events.
options.D: Identify root causes and contributing system or process factors and develop actions to reduce the risk of a similar event recurring.

rationale: Joint Commission's current Sentinel Event Policy states that careful investigation and analysis of patient-safety events and evaluation of corrective actions are essential to reduce risk and prevent harm. Its 2026 Sentinel Event FAQs state that accredited organizations are expected to identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence. D directly reflects that purpose. A substitutes blame for systems analysis, B separates analysis from prevention, and C treats RCA as a reporting-reduction exercise.
educational_objective: Use root cause analysis after a serious safety event to identify root causes and contributing system/process factors and implement improvements that reduce recurrence risk.
source_document_title: Sentinel Event Policy and Procedures; Sentinel Event FAQs

source_locator: Sentinel Event Policy and Procedures — introductory purpose statement and Sharing Sentinel Event-Related Information; Sentinel Event FAQs — 2026 alignment questions stating organizations must examine root causes/contributing factors and make improvements to mitigate recurrence.
source_claim_supported: Root cause/comprehensive systematic analysis is used to investigate root causes and contributing factors and support corrective improvements that reduce risk and prevent recurrence of harm.

source_original.stem: After a wrong-site surgery, a hospital performs a root cause analysis. What is the primary purpose of this process?

options.A: Identify the individual closest to the event and assign direct blame, because personal fault is the main target of a root cause analysis after a sentinel event.
options.B: Document the event for legal purposes without changing care processes, because root cause analysis is separate from efforts to prevent recurrence.
options.C: Determine whether the event can be removed from internal reports, because the main goal is to reduce the number of documented sentinel events.
options.D: Identify underlying system and process factors that contributed to the event and develop actions to reduce the risk of a similar event recurring in the future.

source_original.rationale: Root cause analysis is intended to understand the system and process factors that contributed to a serious event and to guide changes that reduce recurrence. Option D reflects the Joint Commission's current sentinel-event expectations. Option A centers the process on personal blame rather than contributing factors. Option B separates analysis from preventive improvement. Option C treats the process as a reporting-reduction exercise rather than a patient-safety investigation.
source_original.source_detail: The Joint Commission — Sentinel Event FAQs: organizations should identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements/actions to mitigate risk of recurrence rather than focus the analysis on individual blame. Current Joint Commission sentinel-event guidance in 2026; page and current expectations rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, continuity, confidentiality, quality/cost-effective care, legal/ethical rights and assignment/delegation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key and construct. Updated the primary source to the 2026-effective Sentinel Event Policy and current FAQs; tightened D to the exact root-causes/contributing-factors/improvement language used by Joint Commission.

audit_findings.source_authority: Joint Commission current Sentinel Event Policy/FAQs.
audit_findings.currentness: Program-specific policy effective 2026-01-01; current FAQs include May 2026 alignment report references.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Policy purpose/analysis section and current FAQ recurrence-mitigation statements.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final key includes only root causes, contributing factors and preventive improvement; it does not overclaim a mandated analytic method beyond current policy language.

distractor_audit.A: RCA is not primarily a blame assignment exercise.
distractor_audit.B: Prevention/corrective action is integral to the process.
distractor_audit.C: Reporting reduction is not the purpose.
distractor_audit.D: Directly matches current Joint Commission expectation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D describes the current sentinel-event analysis purpose.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are possible organizational goals but only D is source-supported.
audit_findings.blueprint: Quality improvement/event analysis under Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked 2026 policy changes and confirmed the 2027 alignment does not change the current RCA purpose.
